**Distributed Quantum Computing**

In February 2025, researchers at Oxford University demonstrated the first instance of distributed quantum computing. By linking two separate quantum processors using a photonic network interface, they formed a single, fully connected quantum computer. In February 2025, researchers at Oxford University demonstrated the first instance of distributed quantum computing. By linking two separate quantum processors via a photonic network interface, they formed a single, fully connected quantum computer. This breakthrough addresses the scalability challenge in quantum computing, paving the way for systems capable of processing millions of qubits. In July 2025, a collaboration between Cornell University and IBM achieved a significant milestone by demonstrating error-resistant universal quantum gates. Utilizing Fibonacci anyons—exotic quasi-particles—they successfully encoded information through braiding these anyons in two-dimensional space. This method enhances the stability and reliability of quantum computations, moving closer to practical quantum computing applications. ([phys.org](https://phys.org/news/2025-07-error-resistant-quantum-gates-exotic.html?utm_source=openai))
